title: Maria Rodriguez — Enterprise Client Onboarding (Happy Path)
summary: Maria's experience onboarding Apex Solutions, a 200-person financial services firm — her largest single account this quarter. She's energised by the win but frustrated by the CRM admin overhead that pulls her away from relationship work.

actions: Receives deal handover from enterprise deal team
Celebrates the close with her team on the sales floor
laneContent.thoughts: Apex Solutions. Finally. That was a 6-month deal. Now the real work begins — I've got to make sure they actually succeed so this becomes a reference account. And hopefully an upsell.

actions: Opens Salesforce to create the account record
Pulls deal data from the handover sheet (PDF in email)
Manually types contract value, renewal date, key contacts into Salesforce
Assigns account to her region and connects to her open pipeline
laneContent.thoughts: This is the part I hate. I'm copying and pasting from a PDF into Salesforce for 20 minutes. Everything the deal team documented in their system I'm now re-entering in mine. Why can't this just sync?

barriers.description: Deal team uses a different CRM module — no automated handover; Maria manually re-keys 15+ fields
barriers.emergesFrom: Maria's drive for efficiency meets a process that burns time on administration instead of relationship-building — particularly painful because she's just won a deal and wants to be celebrating, not data entering

laneContent.painAtStep: 20 minutes of manual data entry to create a record that should auto-populate from the deal team's Salesforce records. The system is supposed to save time, not create it.
opportunities: One-click account handover: auto-create account record from closed deal record
Progressive CRM enrichment — pre-fill from LinkedIn and contract data

actions: Reviews contract terms and committed success metrics
Researches Apex Solutions on LinkedIn — finds 4 key stakeholders
Calls CS lead to align on implementation timeline
Drafts kick-off agenda and sends to client champion
laneContent.thoughts: The CFO signed the contract but her direct report is the one who'll actually run the implementation. I need to get to him this week before the CS team does — I want to be the face of the relationship, not a handover transaction.
laneContent.needAtStep: An automated stakeholder map that pulls from LinkedIn and the signed contract — so I know who the real decision-makers are before I pick up the phone, not after the first awkward call

actions: Runs 90-minute kick-off on Teams with 6 Apex stakeholders
Agrees communication cadence: monthly calls, shared Slack channel for Tier 1
Identifies Jamie (Head of Ops) as internal champion
Takes structured notes in Salesforce during the call
laneContent.thoughts: Jamie is the one. He's asked three smart questions, he already understands the product, and he's going to be the person who makes this work internally. I need to build that relationship separately from the formal check-ins.
laneContent.needAtStep: A quick way to flag Jamie as 'internal champion' in Salesforce and set up a separate, lighter-touch relationship cadence with him outside the formal account schedule

momentThatMatters.description: Jamie's engagement during the kick-off signals a strong internal champion — Maria recognises this immediately and makes a mental note to invest in that relationship

actions: Updates stakeholder map in Salesforce with 5 contacts and roles
Notes that the CFO (economic buyer) is not attending any implementation calls — flags as risk
laneContent.thoughts: Green on the champion side, amber on the economic buyer. The CFO signed the contract but I've never spoken to her directly. I need a reason to get face time before renewal.

actions: Monitors implementation milestones in Salesforce weekly
Checks in with Jamie via Slack twice a week during implementation
Flags a 2-week delay to CS lead when integration issue emerges
laneContent.thoughts: The integration issue is a risk. Two weeks behind already and we're only in week three. I've flagged it to the CS team but they're saying it's a client-side configuration issue. Jamie is frustrated. I need to own this politically even if I don't own it technically.

barriers.description: No clear escalation path when CS and client disagree on ownership of an integration issue — Maria is caught in the middle
barriers.emergesFrom: Maria's drive to maintain client relationships collides with unclear CS/sales accountability boundaries — she risks being associated with a problem she can't fix

laneContent.painAtStep: The escalation path is unclear. CS says it's the client's IT team's issue; the client's IT team says it's our product. I'm relaying messages and losing credibility with Jamie every time I don't have an answer.

actions: Books 30-day check-in with Jamie and two senior users
Calls CS lead for adoption data before the meeting
Runs the call from her car between two other appointments (mobile)
laneContent.thoughts: CS says they can't share product analytics directly with me — 'not my system'. So I'm going into this call not knowing whether they've actually logged in more than once. I'm going to ask directly and hope it doesn't expose anything.

barriers.description: Product usage analytics are not surfaced in Salesforce — Maria has to request adoption data from CS, who may not respond before the call
barriers.emergesFrom: Maria's relationship-driven approach depends on knowing how the client is using the product — without usage data, she can't personalise the conversation or identify at-risk users before they become a problem

laneContent.needAtStep: Real-time product usage data in Salesforce — which users have logged in, which features they've used, and what they haven't touched yet — so I can personalise every check-in conversation
opportunities: CRM-embedded product analytics dashboard showing per-account and per-user adoption
Pre-call brief that auto-generates from Salesforce health score and usage data

actions: Updates Salesforce health score to Green based on Jamie's positive feedback
Notes that two senior users haven't logged in — flags as minor risk but not escalating
laneContent.thoughts: Green overall but those two non-adopters worry me. If they're not using it after 30 days, they probably won't. I'll mention it gently to Jamie next week.

actions: Prepares value realisation summary with Jamie's input
Identifies a potential upsell opportunity — Apex is expanding into two new regions
Books the call for a Thursday — knows CFO has more availability Thursdays
laneContent.thoughts: The expansion into two regions is interesting. If I can get that upsell on the table before the 90-day review, it frames the renewal conversation differently — it's not 'are you happy' it's 'how do we grow'. That changes the whole dynamic.

actions: Prepares QBR deck with CS input — achievement vs. metrics, roadmap, expansion proposal
Gets CFO in the room for the first time (in-person at Apex offices)
Presents expansion proposal for the two new regions
laneContent.thoughts: Getting the CFO in the room was the goal from day one. The in-person format was the right call — she wouldn't have engaged the same way on Teams. The expansion proposal landed well. She asked about pricing for the new regions. That's a buying signal.
laneContent.needAtStep: A QBR deck template that auto-generates the 'achievement vs. metrics' section from Salesforce data, so I can spend my prep time on the expansion proposal rather than formatting slides

momentThatMatters.description: CFO engages directly in the expansion discussion — first time Maria has had executive access; the QBR format created the right environment

actions: Updates Salesforce: renewal forecast Green, expansion opportunity open
Sends follow-up to CFO with expansion pricing proposal
laneContent.thoughts: Green on renewal, expansion in play. This account is going to finish the year much bigger than it started. That's the job.

actions: Establishes monthly call cadence with Jamie
Quarterly executive touch with CFO
Monitors health score weekly in Salesforce mobile
laneContent.thoughts: The rhythm is set. Jamie is a strong champion. The CFO is engaged. Now I need to convert the expansion proposal and make this a reference account for the financial services vertical.

actions: Logs Apex Solutions as a potential reference account in Salesforce
Nominates them for a case study with marketing
laneContent.thoughts: 90 days in, Green health, expansion in pipeline, CFO access established. I'll take that. If the expansion closes, this is the account story of the year.

outcome.reflection: A smooth onboarding despite early friction with CRM admin and a mid-implementation integration issue. The investment in identifying Jamie as champion paid dividends throughout. Getting CFO access at the 90-day QBR was the defining moment. Expansion proposal in progress.
learnings: Identifying the internal champion early (not just the economic buyer) was critical to navigating implementation issues
In-person QBR created executive access that video calls wouldn't have achieved
CRM admin overhead at account setup burned 45 minutes that should have gone into kick-off preparation

researchSources.source: B2B sales CRM process research and Maria Rodriguez actor development
